title: Settings
introAdmin: These take effect from the next uploaded document, with no server restart. Installation parameters (cores, queue, upload limit) stay in backend/.env.
introUser: Your preferences. The rest of the configuration belongs to your administrator.

max_upload_mb.label: Maximum size of uploadable files (MB)
max_upload_mb.help: Applies to every format: above it, the upload is refused immediately (HTTP 413), before it even reaches the queue.

max_queue.label: Maximum queued jobs
max_queue.help: Above it, uploads answer “queue full” and the user retries later. Queued files live in the server's RAM: raising this raises the memory the queue can take.

xlsx_max_chunks.label: Maximum analysable size (text blocks)
xlsx_max_chunks.help: Sheet content is analysed by the model in blocks of ~120 words: on an office CPU each block costs about 0.75 seconds, so 800 blocks ≈ 10 minutes of processing. Beyond the limit the upload fails with a message stating the file size. 0 = no limit.

xlsx_table_min_rows.label: Minimum rows for per-column anonymisation
xlsx_table_min_rows.help: Cleanly tabular sheets (header + homogeneous columns) with at least this many data rows are anonymised column by column: the model analyses only a sample and PII columns are replaced wholesale, deterministically. Below the threshold (or if the sheet is not tabular) the full analysis is used. 0 = path disabled.

xlsx_table_sample_rows.label: Sample rows per tabular sheet
xlsx_table_sample_rows.help: How many rows (first + spread out + last) go through the model to decide which columns hold PII. More rows = a more reliable decision but a slower analysis.

xlsx_table_coverage_pct.label: Coverage to mark a column as PII (%)
xlsx_table_coverage_pct.help: Minimum share of sampled values recognised as PII for the whole column to be anonymised. Values above 100 are treated as 100.

xlsx_preview_rows.label: Rows per sheet in the preview
xlsx_preview_rows.help: The PDF preview is generated from a copy truncated to this many rows per sheet (the file is shown as a “partial preview”); redaction and residual checks always work on the complete file. Thousands of rows = huge PDFs and slow LibreOffice conversions.

lo_timeout_s.label: Timeout for one conversion (seconds)
lo_timeout_s.help: Maximum time for a single conversion (incoming Office formats and preview PDFs): beyond it, processing fails with “conversion timed out”. Raise it on slow machines if large documents time out.

chat_max_upload_mb.label: Maximum size of a chat attachment (MB)
chat_max_upload_mb.help: A separate (and lower) cap than the one for project files: chat attachments are processed in the sandbox and kept for the whole conversation.

chat_turn_cost_limit_cents.label: Spending cap per single answer (US cents)
chat_turn_cost_limit_cents.help: An answer can cost more than it looks: the model runs code several times and each round re-sends the whole conversation. Once the cap is reached, the model is told to stop running code and answer with what it has (the answer still arrives). 0 = no cap.

chat_model_attach_mb.label: Maximum size of a file sent to the model (MB)
chat_model_attach_mb.help: Images and PDFs are shown DIRECTLY to the model (where supported), so they travel in every request of the turn and are paid for as tokens: above this threshold the file stays in the sandbox only, where the model opens it with code.

chat_web_search.label: Allow web search in chats
chat_web_search.help: Adds two read-only tools to the model (search and page reading) through a browser local to the server. CAREFUL with anonymised chats: search queries leave towards the engine (DuckDuckGo) with the REAL values — the protection covers the path towards the LLM provider, which keeps seeing only placeholders: content fetched from the web comes back anonymised and goes through the egress check. On values not yet known to the registry the protection of web text is best-effort. Every user can turn the search off in a single conversation.

chat_ai_marking.label: Mark AI-generated files (AI Act, Art. 50)
chat_ai_marking.help: Writes a machine-readable English notice into the METADATA of every file the model produces (“AI-generated content”, with the standard IPTC code trainedAlgorithmicMedia): docx/xlsx/pptx in the document properties, PDFs in the Subject and Keywords fields, PNGs in an internal text block, SVGs in a comment. The visible content never changes. csv, json and txt are not marked (a comment would break parsing): for those, the origin recorded by the application applies.

chat_allow_non_zdr.label: Allow models without Zero Data Retention
chat_allow_non_zdr.help: On every request we require Zero Data Retention providers and no data collection; about a third of models have no compliant provider and are refused. With this on, whoever picks one of those models can grant an exception for a SINGLE conversation, with the warning always in view: the provider may keep the data sent and use it to train its models. With it off, nobody can make an exception — not even the administrator.

token_ttl_hours.label: Login session lifetime (hours)
token_ttl_hours.help: Once expired, the user signs in again. Applies to logins made after saving: sessions already open keep their own expiry.

anonDefaults.title: Default anonymisation
anonDefaults.intro: These apply to every user and nobody can turn them off. Categories can be narrowed per project or per chat; terms cannot — anyone can only add their own, under “My terms”.
anonDefaults.policyHelp: You can choose whether to force every user to always run anonymized chats only, or not. With the “Optional” setting, normal chats without the anonymization engine are allowed too.

password.title: Change password
password.intro: You need your current password, no confirmation email. Your session stays open: the new password applies from your next sign-in.
password.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
password.forcedIntro: The administrator requires a password change on first sign-in: choose a new one to continue. Your current password is the one you were given.

myTerms.title: My terms to anonymise
myTerms.intro: Text you always want covered in your projects and chats: client names, internal codes, code names. No other user sees them. They can also be added from the “Anonymise in future too” box when you select text in a preview.
myTerms.globalsTitle: Set by your administrator (they apply to you too)
myTerms.globalsHelp: No need to repeat them here: they are already covered and cannot be turned off.

defaultModel.title: Default chat model
defaultModel.intro: Which model a new conversation starts with. You can pin a specific model or answer three short questions: in that case the actual model is picked when each chat opens, on the current catalogue, and stays for the whole conversation. You can always change it inside the chat.
defaultModel.resolvedNone: Right now no model: you pick one for each new chat.

modelAccess.title: Models visible to users
modelAccess.intro: Which models non-administrator users can see and pick: the whole catalogue, or only the ones selected here. The installation's default model is always included. Administrators always see everything.

tour.title: Tutorial
tour.help: The first-access guided tour: it starts again from the New Chat page and continues on the pages you visit.
